prerequisites: The student must have passed the subjects corresponding to the first two years of the study plan and 30 credits corresponding to the rest of the subjects.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to direct activities that are the object of engineering projects: construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Mechanical Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to organize and plan time.
Oral expression ability.
Written expression ability.
Ability to learn and work autonomously.
Problem-solving ability.
Critical reasoning/logical analysis ability.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Ability to work effectively in a team.
Ability to design and develop projects.
Ability for creativity and innovation.
Motivation for achievement and continuous improvement.
Ability to act ethically and with social commitment.
Ability to evaluate.
Ability to handle technical specifications and to prepare technical reports.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

The student acquires the ability or capacity to: apply the degree's own competences in an integrated manner; write a technical report; make a public presentation; work autonomously and take initiative; express technical information in a foreign language both in writing and orally.

Students learn to face real problems by applying and/or expanding knowledge acquired in their academic training or have direct experience of the technical solutions adopted by a professional or a work group in the exercise of their attributions.
Students learn to value the critical importance of transversal competences and resource management in the efficient functioning of a company.

Students become aware of the discontinuity between the academic university environment and the professional and work environment, so they learn to connect the two spaces and value each of their strengths and weaknesses; this helps the student to smooth the transition between the two realities.

Students gain direct practical experience of the complexity of a real system (e.g., a factory), its constituent equipment, and their monitoring, control, and maintenance needs; similarly, they identify auxiliary systems and the environmental impacts associated with the process and applicable regulations; all of which significantly enriches the academic training received by students in the degree and allows them to integrate content received in different subjects.

Students gain direct practical experience in applying maintenance protocols (corrective, preventive, and predictive) or inspection in industrial processes; they assist in the supervision, repair, or replacement of accessories or equipment, which provides students with very close contact with the external and/or internal constructive structure of representative elements (such as filters, valves, fans, pumps, heat exchangers, turbines, boilers, tanks, deposits, or others).

Students learn to apply routine tools in the operation of a company to solve real problems, which improves their skills in handling regulations, manuals, computer programs (general and specific), plans, reports, technical data sheets for accessories or equipment, technical documentation, catalogs, budgets, and others.

Students gain experience in tasks typical of institutes or organizations linked to research and innovation: design of parts and components, design of elements requiring high precision, use of innovative tools (3D printers), participation in high-level research projects; students learn to value the difficulty of a design and the individual and collective (multidisciplinary) effort required for its viable and practical implementation.

Students participate in the calculation of installations within the activities carried out by an engineering firm, gaining firsthand experience on electrical installations, fire protection, gas or water installations, lighting, ventilation, solar energy installations, and others; they learn to handle regulations and to make the corresponding plans and measurements; these activities, due to their variety and scope, are of great value for the reference framework of any engineering student.

Students learn to develop the commercial and management aspect by having direct contact with suppliers, manufacturers, or the client; these tasks activate interpersonal skills and force students to deal with people on a different level than the purely technical and to adapt their language to their level of understanding (versatility).

syllabus_topics: Knowledge of the organization of professional work in studies, offices, companies, public bodies and industries
Knowledge of the functioning of an industrial process
Ability to plan actions and develop projects
Ability to integrate into a work group, as well as to participate in the assignment of tasks and resources (teamwork)
Ability to analyze, make decisions, and execute solutions
Communication skills, conflict resolution, and negotiation (human resources management)
Motivation for updating, innovation, and research
Ability to handle regulations, equipment manuals, plans, budgets, and other documentation typical of an engineer's activity
Awareness and direct experience of occupational safety and risk prevention
teaching_methods: Practical classes in the classroom for medium or full groups
Attendance at tutorials, in-person and/or virtual, for small groups
Presentation and defense of end-of-subject project
Field internships for full or small groups
Attendance at seminars or activities related to the business, professional, or labor field organized by ESIT, FGULL, or ULL
Visits to local companies and industries

assessment_methods.method: Diary and participation in the monitoring system (SASPE) (as part of E2)
Coordination with the academic tutor (as part of E2)
Oral presentation as a summary of the internships carried out
Attendance at events, seminars or activities related to the business, professional or labor field

assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on: External tutor's report (50%), Internship report, diary, SASPE participation, and coordination with academic tutor (30%), Oral presentation (10%), and attendance at related events (10%). The 30% component is further broken down into: Report (15%), Diary-SASPE (7.5%), Academic tutor coordination (4.5%), and Abstract (3%). For the oral presentation, a minimum grade of 5.0 is required for each aspect (synthesis, communication, content, format, English use), allowing one aspect to be 4.0 if the overall grade is 5.0 or higher; failure results in 'Suspended' with a resit opportunity. Students will be marked 'Suspended' for accumulating three unjustified absences, unauthorized absence, not joining the company on time, not attending scheduled tutorials, repeatedly failing to update their diary, a 'Suspended' grade in the report or oral presentation, not submitting the report or not giving the oral presentation by all deadlines, or not accepting the assigned company without objective reasons. Students not assigned an internship, or those who completed the internship but did not submit the report and/or did not attend the oral presentation (if a resit is possible), will be marked 'Not Presented'. Non-participation in events, seminars, or activities will penalize the E4 component grade.
